label: Code repository
summary: Reads and changes code in a project folder on this computer (a Git checkout).

coreWhy.files.read: Reads the code and its documents.
coreWhy.files.write: Changes code, when you allow it.
coreWhy.shell: Runs Node scripts such as tests and builds, when you allow it.
coreWhy.browser: Opens the changed pages in a browser, when you allow it.

steps: Read the conventions and architecture documents before touching code
Find the existing code, hooks and components that already solve part of it
Make the smallest change that fits the existing architecture
limits: Never invent APIs, files or components you haven't seen in the repository.
Never delete or rewrite unrelated code.
Don't commit or push: the person reviews the changes and commits them.
starters: Look through this repository and describe its structure, stack and conventions. Don't change anything.

questions.label: Conventions or documents it must follow
questions.placeholder: e.g. docs/architecture.md; business logic stays out of components

questions.label: What may it do with the code?

choices.label: Read and explain only
limits: Don't change files: describe the change you'd make.
choices.approval: It can't change files: it reads and explains.

choices.label: Change code
choices.approval: Its changes stay in the working copy until you review and commit them (Changes & versions).

questions.label: Run Node scripts, such as tests and builds
questions.help: Only node and curl commands (for example node node_modules/jest/bin/jest.js). npm, npx and other programs aren't available. Turned off in Inspect workspaces and under a protected-branch policy.

questions.label: Check the result in a browser
questions.help: Opens your local dev server or a site to look at what changed.

questions.label: Commits and pushes
questions.text: Stay yours, from Changes & versions. To let a worker commit through GitHub, register the repository on the GitHub page and grant this worker access in its full definition.

relations.why: Checks the changed pages in a browser.
